name: Beached Sea Creature
summary: Along the windswept coast of Darkshore, the half-devoured remains of a massive sea mammal have washed ashore, guarded by opportunistic murlocs. Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine seeks bone samples from these stranded giants to discern why normally docile ocean beasts are violently dying upon the sands.

sections.title: A Gruesome Shoreline Discovery
sections.body: North along the lonely beaches of Darkshore lies the rotting, half-eaten carcass of a gargantuan sea mammal. Waves crash against its exposed ribs while an unusually vicious tribe of murlocs picks the scavenged bones clean. The sight is both tragic and unnerving, signaling that the ocean's balance is tipping just as severely as the blighted forests inland.

sections.title: Uncharacteristic Stranding
sections.body: According to Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde, the creatures washing up along the strand are typically gentle marine mammals native to the waters surrounding the base of Teldrassil. Unlike aggressive threshers, these gentle beasts have never been known to drive themselves violently onto the rocks. The Temple of the Moon is actively cataloging bone samples to uncover what foul corruption or hidden threat is driving them from the deep to perish on the coast.

faq.q: What kind of creature washed up here?
faq.answer: The skeletal remains belong to a large, gentle sea mammal that usually inhabits the deep, tranquil waters around the base of Teldrassil. They are naturally peaceful giants and are not prone to aggressive behavior or beaching.

faq.q: Why did the sea creature beach itself?
faq.answer: The exact cause is unknown, but Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde notes that such strandings are completely unnatural for this species. Night elf researchers suspect an underlying disturbance or corruption in the surrounding seas is disorienting the creatures or forcing them to flee their native habitats.

Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde is a priestess representing the Temple of the Moon stationed in Auberdine. She is coordinating the ecological investigation into Darkshore's coastline, collecting skeletal remains to study the affliction plaguing the local marine fauna.

faq.q: Why are murlocs gathered around the corpse?
faq.answer: The murlocs are opportunists drawn to the beached giant as an easy, abundant food source. The band surrounding this particular carcass is notably stronger and more aggressive than the murlocs dwelling closer to Auberdine.

faq.q: Where does this creature normally live?
faq.answer: These marine mammals make their home in the open waters encircling the giant boughs and roots of Teldrassil, rarely approaching the mainland shores under normal circumstances.

faq.q: How does this relate to other beachings in Darkshore?
faq.answer: Several marine species have washed ashore along Darkshore, including carnivorous threshers and giant sea turtles. While threshers are naturally turbulent, the beaching of peaceful mammals confirms that the maritime anomaly affects species across the entire coastal ecosystem.

angles.text: The strandings along Darkshore strike a painful chord for the Kaldorei, who revere natural harmony and watch with dread as the waters around their new home of Teldrassil grow troubled.
The Temple of the Moon funds and oversees this inquiry, seeking divine insight into the corruption unsettling Kalimdor's waters.
Any disruption in marine behavior is a dire omen for the Cenarion Circle, pointing toward an unnatural blight poisoning the coastal wildlife.
Securing the shores around Auberdine protects vital Alliance shipping lanes between Darkshore, Teldrassil, and the eastern kingdoms.
